Yeah, I know mechanical relay contacts can weld but that is usually in high voltage/current conditions. The high current is not present when the contactor is first initialized. And mechanical brakes that the operator controls?

It appears that the muni system uses 600 volt DC between the rails and the overhead wires. The major problem with DC is its continuous arcing. It is hard on thyristors and transistors used for motor control. Thyristors often short circuit and the motor then receives power all the time. There has to be a mechanical means of disconnecting power to the drive motor. There also must be circuitry to monitor thyristor failure and shut down the motor power.

Before electronic controls these DC motors were controlled by the use of drum controllers with very large mechanical fingers. There was a large resistor bank on the roof for field voltage control. Motors were shunt wound so that field loss relays kept the motor from running away with loss of field current.
